project.name: Unifi-Log-Insights
project.description: Self-hosted UniFi syslog analyzer: a Python receiver captures syslog over UDP, parses firewall/DHCP/Wi-Fi/DNS/system events, enriches them with GeoIP/ASN/threat intelligence and reverse DNS, stores them in PostgreSQL, and serves everything through a FastAPI backend and a live React/Vite dashboard. Ships as a single supervisord-managed Docker container with a browser extension and an MCP server for AI agents.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start here to understand what UniFi Insights Plus is: a self-hosted analyzer that captures UniFi syslog over UDP, parses and enriches firewall/DNS/DHCP/Wi-Fi events, stores them in PostgreSQL, and serves a live React dashboard. The README lays out the features and installation story, while the architecture wiki page adds nine Mermaid diagrams tracing container startup and the syslog-to-database pipeline. Read these two together to get the mental map the rest of the tour fills in.

tour.title: Receiver Entry Point
tour.description: receiver/main.py is where the backend comes alive. It bootstraps the database, spins up the enrichers and DNS pollers, launches the UDP syslog receiver, and then runs the main service loop that keeps everything ticking. Treat this as the table of contents for the backend: nearly every module in the following steps is imported and wired together here.
tour.languageLesson: This is a long-running Python service, not a request/response app. main.py orchestrates several concurrent workers (syslog socket, pollers, scheduler) rather than returning a value, so the module's job is setup-and-loop, not compute-and-exit.

tour.title: Ingestion and Parsing
tour.description: This is the front door for data. syslog_receiver.py binds a UDP socket (port 514), reads raw UniFi log lines, and writes them to the database in batches with a periodic heartbeat. Each line is handed to parsers.py, which detects the log type and extracts structured firewall, DNS, DHCP, Wi-Fi, and system records from otherwise unstructured text. Together they turn a firehose of syslog strings into typed rows the rest of the system can reason about.
tour.languageLesson: Syslog arrives over UDP, which is fire-and-forget with no delivery guarantee. That is why the receiver batches writes and emits a heartbeat: it optimizes for throughput and observability rather than per-packet acknowledgement.

tour.title: Enrichment and Threat Intelligence
tour.description: Building on the parsed records from Step 3, enrichment.py annotates each log with context: GeoIP location, ASN, AbuseIPDB reputation, and reverse DNS, all behind a TTL cache to respect free-tier API quotas. blacklist.py complements this by pulling external IP blacklist feeds and normalizing them so enrichment can flag known-bad addresses. This is the layer that turns a raw connection log into a security-meaningful event.

tour.title: Data and Persistence Layer
tour.description: Everything ingested and enriched lands here. db/__init__.py is a barrel that re-exports the database submodules as one unified API, and db/core.py is the workhorse: schema management, batched log inserts, threat caching, enrichment-queue operations, and retention cleanup. With a fan-in of 35, db/__init__.py is the single most depended-upon module in the codebase, so understanding its surface pays off across every later step.
tour.languageLesson: The db package uses a barrel __init__.py that re-exports core, config, connection, retention and logs_sql. Callers import from one stable 'db' namespace while the implementation stays split across focused files.

tour.title: The Database Schema
tour.description: init.sql defines the shape of the data the persistence layer writes into. The logs table stores parsed syslog records alongside their geo/ASN/threat enrichment and resolved device names, while ip_threats is a reputation cache keyed by IP. Reading the DDL here makes the enrichment fields from Step 4 concrete and shows the indexes that keep queries fast against millions of rows.
tour.languageLesson: The logs table is denormalized on purpose: enrichment (geo, ASN, threat score) is written inline rather than joined at query time. For an append-heavy analytics workload, this trades storage for read speed, and the heavy index set makes filtered dashboard queries cheap.

tour.title: The HTTP API
tour.description: With data stored, the FastAPI/Starlette app in api.py exposes it. This module wires up CORS, auth middleware, and access-log filtering, then mounts the route modules. The logs, threats, and flows routes are the analytical heart: paginated log listing plus CSV export, batch IP reputation and geo-distribution, and the Sankey/zone-matrix visualizations that power the Flow View. These endpoints are what the frontend in the next steps consumes.

tour.title: Authentication and the MCP Server
tour.description: Two cross-cutting API concerns deserve their own stop. auth.py handles sessions, API tokens, rate limiting, proxy trust, and the login/setup endpoints that gate everything else. mcp.py exposes an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server over JSON-RPC, letting AI agents run scoped log-query and UniFi tools with token scopes and audit logging. This is what makes the project addressable by assistants, not just humans.

tour.title: Integrations and Background Services
tour.description: Beyond raw syslog, the receiver pulls from other sources. unifi_api.py talks to UniFi OS / self-hosted controllers for device-name resolution and firewall syslog management, while pihole_api.py and adguard_poller.py poll Pi-hole and AdGuard Home for DNS query logs and fold them into the same log tables. scheduler.py is the lightweight tick loop that runs periodic jobs like retention cleanup. These run alongside ingestion, orchestrated from main.py in Step 2.

tour.title: Frontend Entry and API Client
tour.description: Now cross to the browser. main.jsx mounts the root App component, which orchestrates tab routing, authentication gating, and global state across the dashboard, flow, log-stream, and settings views. api.js is the glue back to Step 7: a single fetch wrapper with query building, auth-expiry handling, and 80+ typed endpoint functions. With a fan-in of 32, it is the frontend's most central module, so almost every component reaches through it.
tour.languageLesson: api.js centralizes every backend call behind typed functions instead of scattering fetch() calls through components. This gives one place to handle auth expiry and query serialization, and keeps components declarative about what data they need.

tour.title: Dashboards and Visualizations
tour.description: These four components are what a user actually sees. Dashboard.jsx renders summary cards and logs-over-time charts; LogStream.jsx is the live, polling log table with a filter bar; FlowView.jsx composes the Sankey chart, top IP pairs, and zone matrix served by Step 7's flows route; and ThreatMap.jsx plots threat-origin IPs on an interactive geographic map. Each one consumes the enriched data that has flowed all the way from the UDP socket in Step 3.

tour.title: The Browser Extension
tour.description: The optional browser extension brings insights into the UniFi controller UI itself. The MV3 service-worker.js discovers the backend, manages auth tokens, and dynamically registers content scripts on the controller origin. flow-enricher.js then runs in the page: it extracts public IPs from the controller's flow table, asks the background worker for threat data, and injects shadow-DOM threat badges with tooltips. It is a self-contained mini-app that reuses the same API from Step 7.
tour.languageLesson: Manifest V3 extensions replace persistent background pages with an ephemeral service worker, and content scripts use shadow DOM to inject UI (threat badges) into a third-party page without its CSS leaking in or clobbering the host styles.

tour.title: Packaging and Deployment
tour.description: Finally, see how it all ships as one container. The Dockerfile is a multi-stage build: a Node stage compiles the Vite/React UI, then an Ubuntu stage assembles Python, an embedded PostgreSQL, and supervisord to run the receiver and web server together. docker-compose.yml runs that single container, exposing the syslog UDP port and web UI, while .env.example documents every runtime variable and test.yml runs the receiver suite on each push. This closes the loop from source to a running, zero-dependency deployment.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds keep the final image lean: the Node UI-builder stage's toolchain never reaches the runtime image, which carries only the compiled assets. supervisord then acts as a mini init system so one container can run several processes (PostgreSQL, receiver, web server) under a single PID 1.
